rules.title: node_modules (project dependencies)
rules.summary: Installed npm packages of a project; restored with npm install
rules.whatItIs: The installed dependencies of a JavaScript or TypeScript project, as listed in package.json and the lockfile next to it.
rules.whyBig: Every dependency and their dependencies are installed per project; build tools, Electron, TypeScript and native modules make 200 MB to several GB normal.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost if package.json and the lockfile are kept: run 'npm install' (or yarn / pnpm install) to restore it. The project does not run or build until then.
rules.saferAlternative: Delete node_modules of projects you are not working on; reinstall when you return.

rules.title: Dependencies of an installed program
rules.summary: Part of an installed program or tool, not a project; do not delete
rules.whatItIs: A node_modules folder inside Program Files. Here it is part of an installed program or globally installed tool, not a project you can reinstall with npm install.
rules.whyBig: Programs built on Node.js or Electron ship their dependencies this way.
rules.ifDeleted: The program or tool it belongs to stops working until it is reinstalled.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall or update the program it belongs to instead.

rules.title: JavaScript build output (dist)
rules.summary: Build output of a JavaScript project; may be your only copy of a release
rules.whatItIs: The output of a project's build step (bundlers such as Vite, webpack, tsc, electron-builder).
rules.whyBig: Bundles, source maps and packaged apps (installers can be hundreds of MB) accumulate across builds.
rules.ifDeleted: Running the build script recreates it, but a release you shipped is gone if this was the only copy.
rules.saferAlternative: Rebuild with the project's build script when needed; keep released installers elsewhere.

rules.title: JavaScript build output (build)
rules.summary: Build output of a JavaScript project; may be your only copy of a release
rules.whatItIs: The output of a project's build step (Create React App, Electron builds, Docusaurus and others use 'build').
rules.whyBig: Bundles, assets and packaged apps from each build.
rules.ifDeleted: Running the build script recreates it, but a shipped build is gone if this was the only copy. In some projects 'build' holds checked-in build scripts instead.
rules.saferAlternative: Check whether the folder is in version control before deleting it.

rules.title: JavaScript build output (out)
rules.summary: Build output of a JavaScript project (Next.js export, Electron Forge, VS Code extensions)
rules.whatItIs: Output of a project's build: static exports, compiled extension code or packaged Electron apps.
rules.whyBig: Packaged Electron apps and installers can be hundreds of MB per build.
rules.ifDeleted: Running the build recreates it; a shipped build is gone if this was the only copy.

rules.title: Next.js build cache
rules.summary: Next.js build output and cache; recreated by next build or next dev
rules.whatItIs: Build output and cache of a Next.js app, created by 'next dev' and 'next build'.
rules.whyBig: The cache folder grows with every build and development session and can reach GBs.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; the next dev or build run recreates it (slower the first time).

rules.title: Nuxt build folder
rules.summary: Generated files of a Nuxt app; recreated on the next dev or build
rules.whatItIs: Files Nuxt generates during development and builds.
rules.whyBig: Generated code and types.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; Nuxt recreates it.

rules.title: Turborepo cache
rules.summary: Local task cache of Turborepo; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Cached outputs and logs of tasks run with Turborepo.
rules.whyBig: Every cached task output is kept until cleaned.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; tasks run again instead of hitting the cache.

rules.title: Parcel cache
rules.summary: Build cache of the Parcel bundler; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: Parcel's build cache.
rules.whyBig: It grows with every build.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; the next build is slower.

rules.title: Angular CLI cache
rules.summary: Build cache of the Angular CLI; safe to clear
rules.whatItIs: The Angular CLI's persistent build cache.
rules.whyBig: It grows with builds and can reach GBs on large apps.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; the next build is slower.

rules.title: SvelteKit generated files
rules.summary: Generated files of a SvelteKit app; recreated automatically
rules.whatItIs: Files SvelteKit generates during development and builds.
rules.whyBig: Generated code and build output.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; SvelteKit recreates it.

rules.title: Test coverage report
rules.summary: Test coverage report; recreated by running tests with coverage
rules.whatItIs: HTML and data reports produced by test runners (Jest, Vitest, nyc) with coverage enabled.
rules.whyBig: One report per run, overwritten each time.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; run the tests with coverage again.

rules.title: Yarn project cache
rules.summary: Yarn's per-project package cache; sometimes committed on purpose
rules.whatItIs: Package archives Yarn 2+ keeps for a project. In 'zero-install' setups this folder is committed to version control.
rules.whyBig: Every dependency of the project as a zip archive.
rules.ifDeleted: If it is committed, deleting it changes the repository; otherwise 'yarn install' downloads it again.
rules.saferAlternative: Check whether .yarn/cache is tracked in git before deleting.

rules.title: Python virtual environment (.venv)
rules.summary: A project's Python virtual environment; recreate it from requirements
rules.whatItIs: An isolated Python environment for one project, with its own interpreter link and installed packages.
rules.whyBig: Packages like PyTorch, TensorFlow or CUDA libraries are GBs each.
rules.ifDeleted: The project's packages are gone until you recreate the environment (python -m venv .venv, then pip install -r requirements.txt, or 'uv sync' / 'poetry install'). Packages you installed by hand without recording them must be reinstalled from memory.
rules.saferAlternative: Make sure the project lists its dependencies (requirements.txt, pyproject.toml) before deleting.

rules.title: Python virtual environment (venv)
rules.summary: A project's Python virtual environment; recreate it from requirements
rules.whatItIs: An isolated Python environment for one project, with its own interpreter link and installed packages.
rules.whyBig: Packages like PyTorch, TensorFlow or CUDA libraries are GBs each.
rules.ifDeleted: The project's packages are gone until you recreate the environment and reinstall from requirements.txt or pyproject.toml. Packages you installed by hand without recording them must be reinstalled from memory.
rules.saferAlternative: Make sure the project lists its dependencies before deleting.

rules.title: Python bytecode cache
rules.summary: Compiled Python bytecode; recreated automatically
rules.whatItIs: Compiled .pyc files that Python writes next to source files so modules load faster.
rules.whyBig: One small file per module and Python version.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; Python recompiles on the next import.

rules.title: pytest cache
rules.summary: pytest's cache of last-failed tests; safe to delete
rules.whatItIs: pytest's cache, used for options such as --last-failed.
rules.whyBig: Tiny.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks.

rules.title: mypy cache
rules.summary: Type checker cache of mypy; safe to delete
rules.whatItIs: Incremental cache of the mypy type checker.
rules.whyBig: It grows with the code base and the stubs it checks; hundreds of MB on large projects.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; the next mypy run is slower.

rules.title: Ruff cache
rules.summary: Linter cache of Ruff; safe to delete
rules.whatItIs: Cache of the Ruff linter and formatter.
rules.whyBig: Usually small.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost.

rules.title: tox environments
rules.summary: Test environments created by tox; recreated on the next run
rules.whatItIs: Virtual environments that tox creates for each test environment.
rules.whyBig: One full virtual environment per Python version and environment.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; tox recreates them on the next run.

rules.title: Jupyter checkpoints
rules.summary: Jupyter notebook checkpoints; safe to delete
rules.whatItIs: Checkpoint copies of notebooks that Jupyter saves so you can revert to them.
rules.whyBig: One copy per notebook; notebooks with embedded images can be large.
rules.ifDeleted: You can no longer 'Revert to checkpoint'; the notebooks themselves are not affected.

rules.title: Python package metadata (egg-info)
rules.summary: Generated package metadata from setuptools; recreated on build
rules.whatItIs: Metadata that setuptools generates when a package is built or installed in development mode.
rules.whyBig: Tiny.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; a development install ('pip install -e .') may need to be run again.

rules.title: Installed Python packages
rules.summary: Packages installed into a Python environment; remove them with pip
rules.whatItIs: Third-party packages installed into a Python installation or virtual environment.
rules.whyBig: Machine learning and data science packages can be GBs.
rules.ifDeleted: Programs and scripts that use this Python environment fail. If it is inside a virtual environment, deleting the whole environment is cleaner.
rules.saferAlternative: Remove packages with 'pip uninstall' (or delete the whole virtual environment).

rules.title: Unity Library (import cache)
rules.summary: Unity's import cache; regenerated on next open, but reimport can take long
rules.whatItIs: Unity's per-project cache of imported assets, compiled scripts, the package cache and editor state. It is never meant to be committed.
rules.whyBig: Every asset is stored again in its imported, platform-specific form; projects with many textures, models or audio often have 5-50 GB here.
rules.ifDeleted: No project data is lost. The next time you open the project Unity reimports every asset, which can take minutes to hours, and some editor state (window layouts, selection) resets.
rules.saferAlternative: Delete it for projects you are not working on; keep it for active projects to avoid the long reimport.

rules.title: Unity Temp
rules.summary: Temporary files of an open Unity project; deleted when Unity closes
rules.whatItIs: Temporary files the Unity editor uses while the project is open.
rules.whyBig: Builds and imports in progress write here; a crash can leave it behind.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost when Unity is closed; Unity recreates it. Do not delete it while the project is open.

rules.title: Unity project logs
rules.summary: Unity editor and package manager logs for this project; safe to delete
rules.whatItIs: Log files Unity writes for this project (package manager, shader compiler, asset import workers).
rules.whyBig: Logs accumulate with every session.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost.

rules.title: Unity script build intermediates
rules.summary: C# build intermediates of a Unity project; regenerated
rules.whatItIs: Intermediate files from building the project's C# scripts and the IDE project files.
rules.whyBig: Grows with the number of assemblies.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; Unity and your IDE regenerate it.

rules.title: Unity player builds
rules.summary: Built game players; may be the only copy of a release
rules.whatItIs: Player builds you made from this project (the folder name is the common default chosen in Build Settings).
rules.whyBig: Each build contains the whole game, often hundreds of MB to GBs.
rules.ifDeleted: The builds are gone; you can build again from the project, but an exact shipped version may not be reproducible.
rules.saferAlternative: Keep the builds you released elsewhere and delete old test builds.

rules.title: Unity player builds
rules.summary: Built game players; may be the only copy of a release
rules.whatItIs: Player builds you made from this project.
rules.whyBig: Each build contains the whole game, often hundreds of MB to GBs.
rules.ifDeleted: The builds are gone; you can build again from the project, but an exact shipped version may not be reproducible.
rules.saferAlternative: Keep the builds you released elsewhere and delete old test builds.

rules.title: Godot project cache (.godot)
rules.summary: Godot 4 import cache and editor state; regenerated when the project opens
rules.whatItIs: Godot 4's per-project folder with imported assets, shader caches, the global class cache and editor state.
rules.whyBig: Imported textures, meshes and audio are stored again in engine formats.
rules.ifDeleted: No project data is lost; the editor reimports everything on next open, which takes time on large projects, and resets editor layout state.

rules.title: Godot 3 import cache (.import)
rules.summary: Godot 3 imported assets; regenerated when the project opens
rules.whatItIs: Godot 3's folder of imported assets.
rules.whyBig: Imported textures, meshes and audio in engine formats.
rules.ifDeleted: No project data is lost; the editor reimports on next open.

rules.title: .NET build output (bin)
rules.summary: Compiled output of a C# project; rebuilt with dotnet build
rules.whatItIs: Build output of a .NET project (compiled program, libraries and copied dependencies).
rules.whyBig: One subfolder per configuration and target framework (Debug, Release, net8.0, ...); self-contained or published builds include the whole runtime.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost if the source is intact; 'dotnet build' recreates it. Keep it if it is the only copy of a build you shipped.

rules.title: .NET intermediate files (obj)
rules.summary: Intermediate files of a C# build; recreated by restore and build
rules.whatItIs: Intermediate files of a .NET build: compiled objects, generated code, the NuGet restore output (project.assets.json) and incremental build caches.
rules.whyBig: One subfolder per configuration and target framework; large projects and WPF/WinUI apps generate many files.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; the next restore and build recreate it.

rules.title: .NET build output (bin)
rules.summary: Compiled output of an F# project; rebuilt with dotnet build
rules.whatItIs: Build output of a .NET project (compiled program, libraries and copied dependencies).
rules.whyBig: One subfolder per configuration and target framework (Debug, Release, net8.0, ...); self-contained or published builds include the whole runtime.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost if the source is intact; 'dotnet build' recreates it. Keep it if it is the only copy of a build you shipped.

rules.title: .NET intermediate files (obj)
rules.summary: Intermediate files of an F# build; recreated by restore and build
rules.whatItIs: Intermediate files of a .NET build: compiled objects, generated code, the NuGet restore output (project.assets.json) and incremental build caches.
rules.whyBig: One subfolder per configuration and target framework; large projects and WPF/WinUI apps generate many files.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; the next restore and build recreate it.

rules.title: .NET build output (bin)
rules.summary: Compiled output of a VB.NET project; rebuilt with dotnet build
rules.whatItIs: Build output of a .NET project (compiled program, libraries and copied dependencies).
rules.whyBig: One subfolder per configuration and target framework (Debug, Release, net8.0, ...); self-contained or published builds include the whole runtime.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost if the source is intact; 'dotnet build' recreates it. Keep it if it is the only copy of a build you shipped.

rules.title: .NET intermediate files (obj)
rules.summary: Intermediate files of a VB.NET build; recreated by restore and build
rules.whatItIs: Intermediate files of a .NET build: compiled objects, generated code, the NuGet restore output (project.assets.json) and incremental build caches.
rules.whyBig: One subfolder per configuration and target framework; large projects and WPF/WinUI apps generate many files.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; the next restore and build recreate it.

rules.title: Visual Studio solution cache (.vs)
rules.summary: Visual Studio's per-solution cache and user state; recreated automatically
rules.whatItIs: Hidden per-solution folder with IntelliSense databases (Browse.VC.db for C++), the component cache and user options (.suo: open files, breakpoints, startup project).
rules.whyBig: C++ solutions build IntelliSense databases of hundreds of MB to several GB.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing in the code is lost; Visual Studio rebuilds IntelliSense and forgets open documents, breakpoints and the startup project. Close the solution first.

rules.title: NuGet packages folder (packages.config)
rules.summary: Packages restored for older .NET projects; restored again on build
rules.whatItIs: Solution-level folder where NuGet restores packages for projects that use packages.config.
rules.whyBig: Every package version referenced by the solution's projects.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; NuGet restores them on the next build.

rules.title: Rust build output (target)
rules.summary: Rust build artefacts; rebuilt with cargo build
rules.whatItIs: Compiled dependencies, incremental compilation data and binaries of a Cargo project or workspace.
rules.whyBig: Debug builds with incremental data grow quickly; several to tens of GB is common, and old artefacts are never removed.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; 'cargo build' recompiles everything, which can take a while. 'cargo clean' does the same deletion.

rules.title: Maven build output (target)
rules.summary: Maven build output; rebuilt with mvn package
rules.whatItIs: Compiled classes, test reports and packaged artefacts of a Maven project.
rules.whyBig: Packaged JARs/WARs and test output of each build.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; 'mvn package' rebuilds it. Same as 'mvn clean'.

rules.title: Gradle build output
rules.summary: Gradle build output; rebuilt by the next build
rules.whatItIs: Compiled classes, generated sources, intermediates and packaged outputs (APKs, JARs) of a Gradle module.
rules.whyBig: Android modules keep many intermediates; several GB per module is common.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; the next build recreates it. Same as 'gradlew clean'.

rules.title: Gradle build output
rules.summary: Gradle build output; rebuilt by the next build
rules.whatItIs: Compiled classes, generated sources, intermediates and packaged outputs (APKs, JARs) of a Gradle module.
rules.whyBig: Android modules keep many intermediates; several GB per module is common.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; the next build recreates it. Same as 'gradlew clean'.

rules.title: Gradle project cache
rules.summary: Per-project Gradle cache; recreated by the next build
rules.whatItIs: Gradle's per-project cache (file hashes, configuration cache, build output state).
rules.whyBig: Grows with builds and Gradle versions used.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; the next build is slower.

rules.title: Gradle project cache
rules.summary: Per-project Gradle cache; recreated by the next build
rules.whatItIs: Gradle's per-project cache (file hashes, configuration cache, build output state).
rules.whyBig: Grows with builds and Gradle versions used.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; the next build is slower.

rules.title: Android native build cache (.cxx)
rules.summary: CMake/ndk-build intermediates of an Android module; rebuilt
rules.whatItIs: Intermediate files the Android Gradle Plugin creates when building C/C++ code with CMake or ndk-build.
rules.whyBig: One tree per ABI and build variant.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; the next build regenerates it.

rules.title: Android native build cache (.cxx)
rules.summary: CMake/ndk-build intermediates of an Android module; rebuilt
rules.whatItIs: Intermediate files the Android Gradle Plugin creates when building C/C++ code with CMake or ndk-build.
rules.whyBig: One tree per ABI and build variant.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; the next build regenerates it.

rules.title: CMake build folder
rules.summary: Usually a CMake build tree; check for CMakeCache.txt before deleting
rules.whatItIs: Next to a CMakeLists.txt, a folder called build is usually a CMake build tree (it then contains CMakeCache.txt). Some projects keep build scripts under this name instead.
rules.whyBig: Object files, libraries and executables for each configuration; large C++ projects reach many GB.
rules.ifDeleted: If it is a build tree, nothing is lost: reconfigure and rebuild with cmake. If it holds checked-in scripts, project files are lost.
rules.saferAlternative: If it contains CMakeCache.txt it is a build tree and safe to delete.

rules.title: CMake output folder (Visual Studio)
rules.summary: Usually Visual Studio's CMake build output (out/build, out/install)
rules.whatItIs: Visual Studio's CMake integration builds into out\build and out\install by default.
rules.whyBig: Object files and binaries for each configuration.
rules.ifDeleted: If it is build output, Visual Studio regenerates it; check that nothing else is stored in it.

rules.title: CLion CMake build folder
rules.summary: CMake build output created by CLion; rebuilt automatically
rules.whatItIs: Build trees CLion creates per CMake profile (cmake-build-debug, cmake-build-release).
rules.whyBig: Object files and binaries of each profile.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; CLion reconfigures and rebuilds.

rules.title: CMake intermediate files
rules.summary: CMake's internal build files; recreated when CMake runs
rules.whatItIs: Intermediate files and object files CMake generates in a build tree.
rules.whyBig: Object files of every target.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; rebuild with cmake.

rules.title: Dart/Flutter tool cache
rules.summary: Generated files of a Dart or Flutter project; recreated by pub get
rules.whatItIs: Package configuration and generated files of the Dart toolchain.
rules.whyBig: Build caches grow with builds.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; 'flutter pub get' or 'dart pub get' recreates it.

rules.title: Flutter build output
rules.summary: Flutter build output; rebuilt by flutter build
rules.whatItIs: Build output and intermediates of a Flutter app for every platform you built.
rules.whyBig: Android and iOS builds keep many intermediates; GBs are common.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; the next build recreates it. Same as 'flutter clean'.

rules.title: Swift package build folder
rules.summary: SwiftPM build output and checkouts; rebuilt by swift build
rules.whatItIs: Build output and dependency checkouts of a Swift package.
rules.whyBig: Debug builds and checkouts grow with dependencies.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; 'swift build' recreates it.

rules.title: CocoaPods dependencies
rules.summary: Installed CocoaPods dependencies; restored with pod install
rules.whatItIs: Dependencies installed by CocoaPods for an iOS or macOS project.
rules.whyBig: Every pod's sources and frameworks.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost if Podfile.lock is kept; run 'pod install' to restore.

rules.title: PHP Composer dependencies
rules.summary: Installed PHP dependencies; restored with composer install
rules.whatItIs: Dependencies installed by Composer for a PHP project.
rules.whyBig: Every package and its dependencies.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost if composer.lock is kept; run 'composer install' to restore.

rules.title: Terraform working directory
rules.summary: Downloaded Terraform providers and modules; restored with terraform init
rules.whatItIs: Providers, modules and backend settings that 'terraform init' downloads for a configuration. Your state file (terraform.tfstate) is not stored here.
rules.whyBig: Each provider binary is tens to hundreds of MB, per configuration.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; run 'terraform init' again before the next plan or apply.

rules.title: Unreal Intermediate
rules.summary: Unreal build intermediates and generated project files; regenerated
rules.whatItIs: Intermediate files of an Unreal project: compiled C++ objects, generated headers, project files and shader work data.
rules.whyBig: C++ projects build per platform and configuration; several GB is common.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; C++ projects need 'Generate Visual Studio project files' and a rebuild, Blueprint projects regenerate it on open.

rules.title: Unreal project Derived Data Cache
rules.summary: Compiled shaders and processed assets of this project; rebuilt when needed
rules.whatItIs: Project-local Derived Data Cache: compiled shaders, processed textures and other derived data.
rules.whyBig: Grows with assets and target platforms; tens of GB on large projects.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost, but the next open recompiles shaders and rebuilds derived data, which can take a long time.

rules.title: Unreal Saved folder
rules.summary: Logs, crash reports, autosaves, screenshots and local config of the project
rules.whatItIs: Per-project data written by the editor: logs, crash reports, autosaves (Autosaves), screenshots, local config and cooked builds (StagedBuilds, Cooked).
rules.whyBig: Logs, crash dumps, cooked content and staged builds accumulate.
rules.ifDeleted: Autosaves, local editor settings and staged builds are lost; logs and crash reports are only diagnostics.
rules.saferAlternative: Delete Logs, Crashes and old StagedBuilds, but keep Autosaves and Config if you rely on them.

rules.title: Unreal project binaries
rules.summary: Compiled game modules; C++ projects need a compiler to rebuild them
rules.whatItIs: Compiled modules (DLLs and executables) of the project's C++ code and editor targets.
rules.whyBig: Debug builds and multiple targets add hundreds of MB to GBs.
rules.ifDeleted: C++ projects can be rebuilt from source, but only with Visual Studio and the right toolchain installed; without them the project will not open.
rules.saferAlternative: Delete it only if you can rebuild the project's C++ code.

rules.title: Unreal plugin intermediates
rules.summary: Build intermediates of an Unreal plugin; regenerated by the next build
rules.whatItIs: Intermediate build files of an Unreal plugin.
rules.whyBig: Compiled objects per platform and configuration.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing is lost; the next build recreates them.

rules.title: Unreal plugin binaries
rules.summary: Compiled plugin modules; marketplace plugins may ship without source
rules.whatItIs: Compiled modules of an Unreal plugin.
rules.whyBig: One set per platform and configuration.
rules.ifDeleted: Plugins with source can be rebuilt; plugins distributed as binaries only (some Fab/Marketplace plugins) must be downloaded again.
rules.saferAlternative: Check whether the plugin has a Source folder before deleting.

rules.title: Git repository data (.git)
rules.summary: The full history of this repository; deleting it loses all unpushed work
rules.whatItIs: Git's database for this working copy: every commit, branch, tag and stash, plus the index and configuration. Objects are stored compressed in pack files (objects\pack).
rules.whyBig: It grows with history and binary files committed over time; large assets, LFS objects and unreferenced objects from rewritten history add up.
rules.ifDeleted: All history, local branches, stashes and unpushed commits are lost; the folder stops being a repository. Your current files stay.
rules.saferAlternative: Run 'git gc' to repack and remove unreachable objects, 'git lfs prune' for old LFS files, or re-clone if everything is pushed.

rules.title: Git LFS local object store
rules.summary: Local copies of Git LFS files; prune old ones with git lfs prune
rules.whatItIs: Local cache of large files tracked with Git LFS, including old versions you checked out before.
rules.whyBig: Every version of every LFS file you fetched stays until pruned; game and media repositories reach tens of GB.
rules.ifDeleted: LFS files not yet pushed to the server are lost; others are downloaded again on checkout.
rules.saferAlternative: Run 'git lfs prune' to delete old, already pushed LFS objects.

rules.title: Git pack files
rules.summary: Compressed history of a Git repository
rules.whatItIs: Pack files that store a repository's commits, trees and file versions in compressed form.
rules.whyBig: They contain every version of every committed file; committed binaries make them large.
rules.ifDeleted: The repository's history is destroyed; Git can no longer read commits.
rules.saferAlternative: Run 'git gc' or 'git gc --aggressive' to repack, or re-clone a shallow copy if you do not need the history.

rules.title: Blender autosave
rules.summary: Automatic backup of an open Blender scene
rules.whatItIs: Blender's periodic autosave of a scene, written to the temporary folder.
rules.whyBig: As large as the scene.
rules.ifDeleted: You can no longer recover that scene after a crash with File > Recover > Auto Save.

rules.title: Unreal Engine plugin intermediates (engine install)
rules.summary: Part of an Unreal Engine install, not of your project; installed engines cannot rebuild it
rules.whatItIs: Build intermediates (generated headers and build data) of a plugin that ships with Unreal Engine itself.
rules.whyBig: Engine plugins ship generated code and precompiled build data for every platform they support.
rules.ifDeleted: In an engine installed by the Epic Games Launcher, C++ projects that use the plugin can stop compiling until the engine is verified or reinstalled; a source-built engine has to be rebuilt.
rules.saferAlternative: Remove engine versions you no longer use in the Epic Games Launcher instead.

rules.title: Unreal Engine plugin binaries (engine install)
rules.summary: Compiled modules of a plugin that ships with Unreal Engine; part of the engine
rules.whatItIs: Compiled modules (DLLs) of a plugin that ships with Unreal Engine itself.
rules.whyBig: Each plugin ships editor and runtime modules for every platform it supports.
rules.ifDeleted: The editor cannot load the plugin and projects that use it fail to open until the engine is verified or reinstalled.
rules.saferAlternative: Remove engine versions you no longer use in the Epic Games Launcher instead.

rules.title: Part of the Unreal Engine install
rules.summary: Build data of an installed Unreal Engine version; not project output
rules.whatItIs: A Intermediate folder inside an Unreal Engine version installed by the Epic Games Launcher. It belongs to the engine, not to one of your projects.
rules.whyBig: Installed engines ship generated code, compiled modules and build data for their programs and plugins.
rules.ifDeleted: The engine, its tools or C++ projects built against it can stop working until the engine is verified or reinstalled in the Epic Games Launcher.
rules.saferAlternative: Remove engine versions you no longer use in the Epic Games Launcher instead.

rules.title: Part of the Unreal Engine install
rules.summary: Build data of an installed Unreal Engine version; not project output
rules.whatItIs: A Binaries folder inside an Unreal Engine version installed by the Epic Games Launcher. It belongs to the engine, not to one of your projects.
rules.whyBig: Installed engines ship generated code, compiled modules and build data for their programs and plugins.
rules.ifDeleted: The engine, its tools or C++ projects built against it can stop working until the engine is verified or reinstalled in the Epic Games Launcher.
rules.saferAlternative: Remove engine versions you no longer use in the Epic Games Launcher instead.

rules.title: Part of the Unreal Engine install
rules.summary: Build data of an installed Unreal Engine version; not project output
rules.whatItIs: A DerivedDataCache folder inside an Unreal Engine version installed by the Epic Games Launcher. It belongs to the engine, not to one of your projects.
rules.whyBig: Installed engines ship generated code, compiled modules and build data for their programs and plugins.
rules.ifDeleted: The engine, its tools or C++ projects built against it can stop working until the engine is verified or reinstalled in the Epic Games Launcher.
rules.saferAlternative: Remove engine versions you no longer use in the Epic Games Launcher instead.

rules.title: Part of the Unreal Engine install
rules.summary: Build data of an installed Unreal Engine version; not project output
rules.whatItIs: A Saved folder inside an Unreal Engine version installed by the Epic Games Launcher. It belongs to the engine, not to one of your projects.
rules.whyBig: Installed engines ship generated code, compiled modules and build data for their programs and plugins.
rules.ifDeleted: The engine, its tools or C++ projects built against it can stop working until the engine is verified or reinstalled in the Epic Games Launcher.
rules.saferAlternative: Remove engine versions you no longer use in the Epic Games Launcher instead.

rules.title: Installed Python package metadata (egg-info)
rules.summary: Metadata of an installed Python package; pip and Python need it
rules.whatItIs: The metadata of a package installed into a Python environment: its name, version, files and entry points.
rules.whyBig: Usually small; it lists the files the package installed.
rules.ifDeleted: pip no longer sees the package, so it cannot be upgraded or uninstalled cleanly, and code that looks up its version or entry points fails.
rules.saferAlternative: Remove the package with 'pip uninstall' instead.

rules.title: Python standard library: venv module
rules.summary: Part of a Python installation (the module that creates environments)
rules.whatItIs: The 'venv' package of the Python standard library, which creates virtual environments. It sits next to os.py and the other standard modules.
rules.whyBig: Small; some distributions add launcher executables.
rules.ifDeleted: Python can no longer create virtual environments ('python -m venv' fails), and tools that rely on it break.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall or repair the Python installation it belongs to instead.

rules.title: Python environment of an installed program
rules.summary: Part of an installed program or tool, not a project; do not delete
rules.whatItIs: A Python virtual environment inside Program Files. Here it holds the Python packages an installed program runs on, not a project environment you can recreate.
rules.whyBig: Programs that bundle Python (AI tools, launchers, editors) ship their packages this way, often several GB.
rules.ifDeleted: The program it belongs to stops working until it is reinstalled or repaired.
rules.saferAlternative: Uninstall or update the program it belongs to instead.
